4-Bet Call

As we saw in Chapter 9, this range is
not necessarily ahead when the action
goes open, 3-bet, 4-bet, shove, call; but
each hand within it is +EV to 4-bet and
call a shove with. AKo, for example,
makes up for a slight deficit in equity vs.
a tight 3-bet/shoving range of [QQ+
AK] by picking up dead money and
blocking the hands that crush it.

I recommend [QQ+ AK] as a standard
4-bet/call range CO vs. blinds. In a more
aggressive spot like CO vs. BU, BU vs.
SB, or SB vs. BB; this can be widened
```

4-Bet/Fold

This is Hero's 4-bet bluffing range and
consists of the hands that block Villain's
3-bet/shoving range the best, preferring
playability where blocker power is
equal. KJo is of course not suited, but its
double blocker potential renders it a
more suitable 4-bet bluff than something
like K7s. It's likely that JJ will form a
part of Villain's 3-bet/shoving range,
while 77 will not and so the J is the
more useful blocker to hold. Also note
that [A2s-A5s] has been chosen before
```
